What is Cloudflare Tunnel? A beginner's guide to using it, setting up a home server, and connecting via SSH.

    Tsunku @ Useful Tools
    September 15, 2026 20:28

    Cloudflare Tunnel is a mechanism that allows you to connect your home server, company server, etc., to Cloudflare without directly exposing your public IP address or incoming ports.

    It's used in situations such as wanting to view a website running at home from outside, temporarily checking an application under development, or securely connecting to a server via SSH.

    This article explains the Cloudflare Tunnel mechanism, basic usage, hosting a home server, SSH connection, Quick Tunnel, and troubleshooting points. We will focus on the basics of Tunnel, leaving detailed Zero Trust policy design and Minecraft-specific settings for separate topics.

    What is Cloudflare Tunnel?

    Cloudflare Tunnel runs a program called cloudflared on the server side to create an outbound connection to the Cloudflare network.

    Normally, connecting to your home server from outside requires opening ports on your router and checking your global IP address. With Tunnel, the server initiates the connection to Cloudflare, allowing you to publish your app via Cloudflare without opening incoming ports to the internet.

    According to Cloudflare's official explanation, Tunnel does not use publicly routable IP addresses, and Cloudflared uses this mechanism to create outbound connections to Cloudflare.

    The communication flow can be thought of as follows:

    利用者
  ↓ HTTPS
Cloudflareのホスト名
  ↓ Tunnel
cloudflared
  ↓ localhost:8000など
自宅・社内のアプリ

    By reducing incoming connections to the origin server, it becomes more difficult to create paths that allow direct access to the IP address. However, simply configuring a tunnel does not mean that authentication and vulnerability countermeasures for public applications are fully completed.

    What you can do with Tunnel

    Typical uses are as follows:

    • Publish a web application on your home server.

    • Temporarily share the localhost during development.

    • Connect to the company's HTTP service.

    • Create an entry point for SSH connection.

    • Connect to a remote desktop, etc.

    • Restricting users in conjunction with Cloudflare Access

    • Create a route to the private network

    The settings will differ between publicly accessible applications and internal applications used only by specific users. For websites accessible to everyone, use the public hostname; for administration panels or SSH, consider adding authentication such as Access.

    Things to prepare in advance

    To create a standard remote management tunnel, you will need the following:

    • Cloudflare account

    • Domains managed by Cloudflare

    • Servers and PCs that run the application

    • Install Cloudflared on the server

    • Communication from the server to the internet.

    • The local URL and port number of the app to be published.

    Cloudflare's official setup guide requires a Cloudflare domain to publish your app. In environments with strict firewalls, you should also verify that your server can connect to Cloudflare on port 7844.

    Steps to create a Tunnel from the Dashboard

    The basic procedure is as follows. Since the menu names on the Dashboard may change, please prioritize the official screen when working.

    1. Log in to the Cloudflare Dashboard.

    2. Open Tunnels from Networking

    3. Select "Create a tunnel".

    4. Enter the tunnel name.

    5. After creation, select the server's OS.

    6. Execute the displayed installation and authentication commands on the server.

    7. Verify that the Tunnel is healthy.

    8. Add the root directory for the app you want to publish.

    9. Set the hostname and Service URL.

    10. Verify functionality from an external browser.

    For the Service URL, specify the URL of the application that is visible from the server where Cloudflared is running, for example, http://localhost:8000. If the application is on a different PC, specify the private IP address and port that can be reached from the server.

    Adding a public hostname means that requests to that URL will pass through the Tunnel and reach your local app. Even if your app is bound only to localhost, you can configure it to be reachable from Cloudflare on the same server.

    Precautions when using a home server

    A major advantage of using Tunnel with a home server is that it reduces the number of open ports on your router. However, since this increases the number of paths entering your home network, you should keep the services you expose to a minimum.

    The items you should check are as follows:

    • Have you updated your OS and apps?

    • Is the administration panel exposed to the internet?

    • Are you using strong passwords and multi-factor authentication?

    • Are you opening any unnecessary ports on your router?

    • Will the Tunnel recover after the server is powered off or restarted?

    • Do you know how to check logs and how to deal with failures?

    • Could it be possible to unintentionally reach other devices in the home?

    Tunnel is a mechanism for managing external entry points and does not replace authentication for the application itself. For the admin panel, SSH, and database, you should decide how to restrict users before creating public hostnames.

    When using an SSH connection

    SSH is a crucial gateway for server management. When connecting via SSH through a tunnel, you need to not only create a public hostname but also verify the user authentication method and Cloudflared's settings.

    When using SSH, combine the following measures:

    • Do not allow password logins more than necessary.

    • Use SSH keys and do not give your private key to others.

    • Avoid direct login as root.

    • Restrict the users who can connect.

    • Restricting users with Cloudflare Access, etc.

    • Check the connection log.

    SSH settings vary depending on the OS, client, and Cloudflare Access configuration. Rather than simply copying commands, it's best to configure your settings by comparing the official SSH connection procedure with your own authentication method.

    What is Quick Tunnel?

    Quick Tunnel is a feature that allows you to temporarily access and view your locally running web server from an external source. A random subdomain of trycloudflare.com is issued, allowing you to briefly share a page you are developing.

    While convenient for testing, the official documentation states that Quick Tunnel is intended for testing and development purposes and is not recommended for production use. Because anyone with the URL could potentially access it, avoid using it in apps containing personal information, administration panels, or sensitive data.

    Once the temporary check is complete, stop the process and verify that no shared URLs or credentials remain. For the production site, use named tunnels or remote management tunnels to organize domains, authentication, and monitoring.

    How to use it in conjunction with BlogStar

    When organizing your home server configuration, deployment procedures, and update schedule into articles, you can use BlogStar , which uses AI to streamline blog post creation and management, to organize your work notes. Do not paste Tunnel tokens or SSH private keys into your articles or notes.

    Common errors and how to check them

    The Tunnel is not healthy.

    Verify that Cloudflared is running, that the authentication commands are correct, and that the server can communicate outwards. Firewalls or proxies may be blocking communication to port 7844.

    This results in a 502 error or connection error.

    Even if the Tunnel itself is connected, there could be reasons such as the application in the Service URL being stopped, the port number being incorrect, or localhost pointing to the wrong destination. First, check if you can access the Service URL from the server.

    It becomes 522

    Check the public hostname, DNS, Tunnel root, and Service URL in that order. If connecting to an HTTPS origin, also check if the certificate and redirect conditions are correct.

    summary

    Cloudflare Tunnel is a mechanism that creates an outbound connection from Cloudflare to Cloudflare, allowing you to expose and connect your home or company services via Cloudflare.

    While this reduces the number of exposed incoming ports, Tunnel alone does not guarantee authentication or application security. You should limit the services you expose and set up additional authentication for the management interface and SSH.

    First, test the system with Quick Tunnel, and then in production, set up named tunnels, custom domains, authentication, monitoring, and recovery procedures.

    For the latest setup instructions, please refer to the official Cloudflare Tunnel documentation , the creation procedure from the Dashboard , and the official Quick Tunnel guide .
